statusMeanings.PASS: Every evidence slot the derivation rule requires is present and exists in this tree, and the row carries no evidenceGap. Says nothing about production fitness beyond what the cited evidence covers.
statusMeanings.PARTIAL: The mechanism exists and something in this tree gates it, but at least one required evidence slot is missing or a named gap remains. The gap is always named in evidenceGap.
statusMeanings.FAIL: A user-visible capability is known to be broken, or the evidence needed to claim it is absent while the defect it would have caught has already shipped. A FAIL row is a finding, not a placeholder.
statusMeanings.NOT_APPLICABLE: A decided, recorded exclusion with its reason. Never used for work that is merely unwritten.

derivation.method: Status is derived from what exists in this tree and what the gates actually assert, not from prose. A row is PASS only when every slot below is present AND exists AND evidenceGap is empty; anything else is PARTIAL with the missing slot named, unless a user-visible defect is known, in which case FAIL.
passRequires: oracleFixtures: at least one recording of pinned behaviour that the row's differential compares against
implementation: at least one Go file or package that carries the behaviour
tests: at least one named test that fails when the behaviour is wrong (existence checked, and the name must resolve to a real test function or harness file)
ci: at least one workflow job that runs that test
derivation.productionRule: AGENTS.md 22 and 29-30: a behaviour verified only against our own mock peer is `unverified` for production. Such rows cannot be PASS no matter how complete the fixture is, and the gap says so verbatim.
derivation.artifactRule: AGENTS.md 23 and 34: a release claim needs the shipped artifact, unpacked, started against a stock tree. Rows whose only evidence is the source tree carry that gap until a release-artifact result exists.
derivation.failRule: AGENTS.md 40: a defect that shipped is recorded here even after it is fixed, because the row's status is about the evidence layer that allowed it through. A fixed mechanism promotes a row from FAIL only when the gate that would have caught it exists and has run.

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: this row stays FAIL, but it is no longer true that nothing observes the client carrying user traffic: the subprocess test boots the shipped binary and asserts at the recording peer that the provider request arrived with the production client's own fingerprint (accept-encoding exactly `gzip`, no Connection header, canonical header names) and that the captured provider body arrived byte-identically. absentGate.mustAssert: a controlled peer that behaves like the internet: a local TLS listener with a real trust chain, a refusing proxy, and a socket that accepts then never answers — each asserted to produce a NAMED causal error (DNS, connect, TLS, proxy, timeout) with no secret in it, through the shipped artifact

evidenceGap: every provider differential runs against our own recording peer: AGENTS.md 22 makes that `unverified` for production

no test asserts the causal error text of a DNS, connect, TLS or timeout failure without printing a secret (AGENTS.md 35)

the live canary that does reach api.deepseek.com runs only where DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is configured, and prints one SKIPPED line where it is not

rows.area: Streaming SSE framing, incremental render and cancellation

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: the row's claims about streaming sse framing, incremental render and cancellation rest on this test; deleting or weakening it makes the row unsupported, and the checker fails a row whose named test does not exist

evidenceGap: a mid-stream TLS close is unobserved: the fault is a socket close on plain HTTP, so a TLS fatal alert or a middlebox reset is not reproduced (the gzip decoder error stands in for the artifact of a truncation and IS measured, in tests/browser/streaming-framing-hop-selftest.mjs)
several cancellation artefacts record the partial text at the moment of abort, which is a per-run observation; no gate asserts the ordering property itself
rows.notes: Streaming has the deepest browser instrumentation in the tree (frame-by-frame render alignment on both legs). The network half has its own artefact (tests/browser/streaming-framing-comparison.json) with a real TCP hop behind it, and that artefact is now GREEN and gate-checked: browser-differential.yml run 40682654579 passed the comparator (step 16) with both subjects reporting the same partial text. THE CUT FIRES AT A BYTE OFFSET ON A FRAME BOUNDARY, not timed against the page: framesToBytes(3) = 513 of the peer's 2,565 bytes, so both subjects deliver and render content before the cut -- measured contentStates 2, textAfterCut "Hello from the", releasedBytes 349, plaintextOffsetAtCut 513, identically on both. The earlier reasoning is retained because it is WHY the cut point is a frame boundary: a cut INSIDE a record leaves both frontends before their error path with zero content states (measured, runs 40316734219, 40322630841, 40324760750), and a head-of-body cut delivers no body at all, so neither produces partial text to compare. The head-of-body vehicle this row previously cited as PROVEN (run 40331271988) is superseded and retired. Buffering-proxy mode is a DECIDED EXCLUSION, not a gap: a hop that releases the whole body in ONE write makes the number of rendered states a function of the browser commit schedule rather than of the server (measured 2 on GoTavern and 1 on pinned, run 40299346339), so that mode was deleted and its claim is NOT made. Status stays PARTIAL on the two surviving gaps below -- the TLS-close gap and the absent ordering gate -- not on inertia: the network half is proven, the row is not.

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: no gate exists: docs/startup-state-machine.md §2 lists the unbounded waits and no test bounds them, so a stock-tree hang would go red nowhere. The gate that must land is a boot with a wall-clock bound per wait, against a real SillyTavern directory, failing with the wait named.

absentGate.mustAssert: a boot over a stock SillyTavern directory completes inside a wall-clock bound, with every wait in docs/startup-state-machine.md §2 individually bounded and its bound named in the failure, and the tree left unmodified

evidenceGap: P0-B: a boot inside a real SillyTavern directory hung; docs/startup-state-machine.md §2 lists the unbounded waits (flock acquisition, resolver call, sleep loop, join without producer) and no gate bounds them (AGENTS.md 24)
no gate asserts that startup makes no non-essential network access (AGENTS.md 25)
no gate asserts that a parseable config is never rewritten as a side effect (AGENTS.md 27)
every startup fixture starts from a fresh or migrated runtime root, never from a stock SillyTavern tree that a user already runs

DUPLICATE-KEY CONFIG: pinned refuses it by name and does NOT rewrite the file (measured, tests/oracle/sillytavern-1.19.0-config-duplicate-key.json): exit 1, 'Could not add missing config values ... YAMLParseError: Map keys must be unique at line N, column M' with code DUPLICATE_KEY, then 'FATAL: Failed to read config.yaml. Please check the file for syntax errors.', and the file's bytes and mtime are IDENTICAL before and after (sha256 0f0ee0ee/57cdc75f both sides). The control -- the same document minus the duplicate -- boots AND is migrated (25 -> 3310 bytes), which is what makes 'untouched' readable rather than vacuous. THE USER-VISIBLE STORY IS THE GOOD ONE: they can fix the duplicate and restart with nothing lost, rather than having their config rewritten on the way to a crash. GoTavern currently ACCEPTS a duplicate key where pinned exits 1, so the divergence runs in the direction of being more permissive; that is recorded here rather than asserted as parity, and TestDuplicateKeyIsAcceptedWherePinnedRejectsIt is the test that names it
rows.notes: The state machine is documented in detail and the invariants are written into AGENTS.md 24-28; what does not exist is a test that fails when a wait is unbounded or a stock tree hangs. That absence is the defect the process is missing (AGENTS.md 40).

rows.notes: This is the row this lane exists to create, and it is honestly FAIL today: most of the harness still covers its steps as independent experiments. One leg now carries state (see the first evidence gap), which is one of four things this row needs; the row stays FAIL until the other three exist. Section `session` records the per-step inventory that supports that claim.

session.purpose: The whole-session differential AGENTS.md 34/38 asks for, inventoried against the harness that exists. It proves the claim above: every step has a probe, no probe shares a runtime with another, so there is no session.

steps.userAction: open the pinned frontend root in a browser
open a chat and see its history
send a message and receive a completion
send with streaming on, then cancel mid-stream
reload the page and see the conversation back
steps.notImplemented: no probe reads state back through the frontend after a reload; chats-save-get compares the HTTP round trip, not the browser's rehydration

canonicalisation.method: Each step's observation is compared after replacing those four classes with markers by FIELD PATH, never by regex over the whole document, and the replacement is recorded beside the observation so it cannot be silently widened. Byte equality is never claimed for a field that carries a clock.
forbidden: sorting arrays whose order is the contract
